rule: Establish proportions and sizes in a simple diagrammatic sketch first; errors there carry through to the finished drawing.
Place the darkest accents on a portrait only at the eyes, nose, mouth, around the ear and under the chin; misplaced accents ruin the drawing.
Break a subject down into a few simple values before rendering; the white paper counts as one of the values.
Draw objects with as few lines as possible, choosing the lines that explain the form, and use overlap and perspective to show depth.
Spot solid blacks early; they give a reference for judging the gray values and separate the elements.
The paper surface changes line and tone quality; rough paper breaks up darks, smooth paper gives crisp lines and a full tonal range.
